transcription.notes: Counts: read/R*.raw.txt holds one output per cipher token (dec.py), and the per-letter counts equal those of parse.py on DECODE's DOC_R*.txt files (git-ignored img/, 3504 tokens, 252 distinct in all). DECODE's transcription slips pass into the machine reading as {..} or nonsense syllables; no corrections against the images were made.

system.summary: Point-separated syllabic nomenclator: numbers 9-30 single letters, 31-60 consonant-vowel syllables in rows of five, struck numbers a second syllable table, letter pairs as syllables with the consonant disguised, about twenty three-letter code words, struck nulls.

diacritics.note: A stroke through a number selects the second syllable table (DECODE marks it '+'); struck N, R, g, 4 are nulls.

system.notes: distinct_symbols counted with parse.py over DECODE's DOC_R*.txt (git-ignored). Struck 14 is not fixed (possibly 'ju'); tan (Flandes?) and cun iles (españoles?) are conjectural. 116 = V.S.; 8 is used for o.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherments in the left margin of all ten letters (eight recognised by DECODE; faint ones on R1004/R1005 found during this work)

conditions.human_role: Supplied the DECODE login (session cookie) for the transcriptions and images.

solution.what: Fetched DECODE R1002-R1011 images and DECODE's DOC_*.txt ciphertext transcriptions with the stored cookie.
parse.py token counts over the ten transcriptions; n, r, s (20, 24, 25) the commonest tokens.
Lined the 4 Sept letter (R1010) up against its marginal decipherment; the key structure (letters 9-30, syllables 31-60, struck table, disguised letter pairs, code words) followed.
Applied the rebuilt key (dec.py) to all ten transcriptions, including R1004 and R1005 listed as non-decrypted.
Faint marginal decipherments on R1004 and R1005 found and compared; they agree with the key reading. The key reproduces the other eight margins.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 3366 tokens, 192 types, es-golden-age order 4: reading -2.259 per letter; random keys -4.152 (z 8.2); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.63 (mean -2.655, z 29.8); annealer on the real text -2.559. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): DECODE ciphertext transcriptions (DOC_*.txt, previously only in the git-ignored img/) copied to decode/; decryptions are the machine readings read/R*.raw.txt (dec.py), plus the normalised R1004/R1005 text copied from NOTES; key table copied from NOTES to texts/key.md. The contemporary margin decipherments of the eight are not transcribed.

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test): read/R*.raw.txt and texts/R1004_R1005_normalised.md read through. Only R1004 and R1005 have a normalised Spanish text; the other eight are raw syllable streams with stray letters and DECODE slips, and their margin decipherments were never transcribed. The eight relabelled decoded, not read; class read -> read in part; fraction_read 0.961 -> 0.121.

Margins transcribed: the contemporary left-margin decipherments of R1002, R1003, R1006-R1011 read from the DECODE images (scratchpad, not in the repo), checked against DECODE's partial margin transcriptions, and aligned word by word with the key decode; each letter written as normalised Spanish (read/R*_reading.md) and translated (read/R*_en.md); R1004/R1005 translated too. Code words fixed from the margins: cen = Duque, ren/xen = gobierno, xin = gente, cun = España, tin = Francia, gen = enemigos, {110} = cuando, struck 14 = ju, pa+55 = Papa. Eight letters relabelled read; class read in part -> read; fraction_read 0.121 -> 1.0.

Print search: web searches for a printed edition of Carpio's 1677 Rome letters to Baltasar de Fuenmayor (Spanish envoy in Denmark) found none; Carpio's Roman embassy is studied for his art collecting, and a UNED study of Spain-Denmark diplomatic agents 1640-1680 was found but could not be opened.
Verification 5 (plain-bar rows): read/R1006_reading.md had no ## Reading heading (header and notes scored, plain 0.529); heading added, body plain 0.778, explicit 0.889. Keeps read.

R1006 reading: the modernised spelling of 22 Oct restored to the writer's from the margin decipherment (read/R1006_margin.txt), accents off, holes kept, no word changed ([?Hyères] -> [?Vieres] as written); rescored with research/reading_audit/v2_score.py: plain 0.778 -> 0.556 (period spelling against a modern word list), explicit holes 0.889 unchanged. Keeps read on the explicit-hole share.

v6 spelling check (23 Oct 2026, research/reading_audit/v6_spelling_files.txt): the modernised spelling of 22 Oct restored to the writer's, word by word from the contemporary margin decipherments as transcribed (read/R*_margin.txt; research/reading_audit/v6_align.py), editorial accents off, words the margin does not carry spelt as the key decode gives them; abbreviations and code words written out; holes and brackets kept, no word changed (R1006 left to the agent working on it). Rescored with research/reading_audit/v2_score.py: read/R1002_reading.md plain 0.655 -> 0.517, explicit holes 0.931 -> 0.931; read/R1003_reading.md plain 0.75 -> 0.45, explicit holes 0.95 -> 0.95; read/R1007_reading.md plain 0.818 -> 0.818, explicit holes 0.909 -> 0.909; read/R1008_reading.md plain 0.8 -> 0.7, explicit holes 1.0 -> 1.0; read/R1009_reading.md plain 0.8 -> 0.65, explicit holes 0.95 -> 0.95; read/R1010_reading.md plain 0.765 -> 0.529, explicit holes 1.0 -> 1.0; read/R1011_reading.md plain 0.744 -> 0.615, explicit holes 0.949 -> 0.949. The plain share falls with period spelling against a modern word list; the explicit-hole share, the bar for period spelling, is unchanged or the change comes from the new header lines in files without a '## Reading' heading. outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The syllabic nomenclator was rebuilt by lining up the 4 Sept letter (R1010) with its contemporary marginal decipherment and then applied to all ten DECODE transcriptions; the reported text is the key's output, checked against the margins (the faint margins on R1004/R1005 were found after the key had read them).
outcome.fraction_read_source: 22 Oct 2026, after the margins were transcribed: all ten letters build sentences and are translated (read/R*_reading.md, read/R*_en.md, texts/R1004_R1005_normalised.md). Tokens in letters that read / all tokens = 3,504 / 3,504 (document lengths in documents[]). Holes inside the read letters are a handful of words: R1002 one bracketed group, R1003 one supplied verb, R1006 two uncertain place names, R1009 one supplied word; plus DECODE placeholders ({>}) in R1009/R1011 that carry no text.
outcome.notes: Key rebuilt here from the letters with the marginal decipherments (complete, contemporary) in hand, so attack is archive decipherment rather than cryptanalysis. Open in the key: struck 14 and a few struck numbers ([55], [25], [80], ...); three code words conjectural. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: the eight margined letters relabelled decoded, not read (raw syllable streams; their margins, the readings of record, are not transcribed); class read -> read in part. 22 Oct 2026, later: the eight margins transcribed from the images and aligned with the key decode; each letter normalised (read/R*_reading.md) and translated (read/R*_en.md); class read in part -> read.

texts.label: R1010, Rome 4 Sept 1677

reading_review.note: Two clear paragraphs: the French fleet from Messina aims at Catania, not Brindisi; Orange raised the siege of Charleroi. Key decode and DECODE margin transcription agree; one word corrected (temer). Verified word by word 22 Oct 2026: 0 words bracketed (0 supplied, 0 partly carried), 0 replaced. Margin transcribed from the images to read/R1010_margin.txt 22 Oct 2026; re-checked against it: 0 bracketed, 0 replaced.

texts.summary: Carpio to Fuenmayor: The French fleet has left Messina; rumoured bound for Brindisi, its design is to surprise Catania, and its good fortune makes any operation it undertakes to be feared. Carpio is dismayed by news from Brussels that the Prince of Orange raised the siege of Charleroi "intempestivamente".
texts.note: The reading is the key decode (decryption) normalised word by word against the contemporary margin decipherment, transcribed from the DECODE images on 22 Oct 2026; translation in English.

texts.label: R1011, Rome 18 Sept 1677

reading_review.note: Continuous prose on the anti-Spanish riots in Rome, the militia and guns at Sant'Angelo, and the French galleys' press-gang at Civitavecchia; margin read from the images and aligned with the key. Two readings where margin and key differ are noted. Verified word by word 22 Oct 2026: 7 words bracketed (4 supplied, 3 partly carried), 0 replaced. Margin transcribed from the images to read/R1011_margin.txt 22 Oct 2026; re-checked against it: 0 bracketed, 0 replaced (the margin carries the earlier-bracketed trata/de and Civitavecchia; brackets kept; "pasando" and "sin reservar" kept with the key where the faint margin may read "pensando", "con reservar").

texts.summary: Carpio to Fuenmayor: After Charleroi, rumours that Spaniards were raising men by force for Sicily turned the Roman populace against them; Spaniards have been insulted and stoned in the streets for over fifteen days with no action from the Pope, while militia cavalry was brought in and guns added on Castel Sant'Angelo. Carpio contrasts the tolerance shown to the French, whose galleys pressed more than a hundred men, reapers included, at Civitavecchia.

texts.label: R1004, Rome 13 Nov 1677
texts.summary: Carpio to Fuenmayor: Carpio laments Spain's ill fortune: the Cardinal d'Estrées's arrival at Turin threatens some novelty in Italy and Flanders is in the state Fuenmayor knows; the Congress must wait on the Prince of Orange's meeting with the King of England; the King's orders have not yet come. DECODE lists it as not decrypted; a faint margin decipherment agrees with the key.

reading_review.note: texts/R1004_R1005_normalised.md is continuous Spanish (d'Estrées at Turin, Orange and the King of England, the orders from Madrid) and agrees with the faint margin decipherment; the raw file is the syllable stream behind it.
